messages:
ops_bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: hosted-runtime-17 reported sustained OOMs on kvcache shard pool-3. Memory growth correlated with continuous-batching requests. Auto-pager sent to #incidents.

sre_pager: I'm on it, grabbing logs + stack traces. Any customer-facing impact yet?

prod_support_kim: Already seeing a handful of 500s from customers on hosted tenant `acme-proxy`. Severity P1 if it keeps up.

eng_runtime_amy: Noted — this looks similar to previous runaway context cases but not identical. I'm pulling the kvcache metrics and request traces now.

ml_oncall_rajesh: Paging in. Can you share top offending request IDs? I'll check kv cache keys and batch sizes.

ops_bot: Top traces (shortened):
```
TRACEID: 0a1b2c - model: redwood-7b-quant - req_tokens: 134k - batch_size: 128 - kv_entries: 2.1M - mem: 62GB
TRACEID: 0a1b2d - model: redwood-7b-quant - req_tokens: 210k - batch_size: 64 - kv_entries: 3.8M - mem: 68GB
TRACEID: 0a1b2f - model: redwood-13b - req_tokens: 95k - batch_size: 256 - kv_entries: 1.7M - mem: 55GB
```

eng_runtime_amy: Whoa — requests with req_tokens >100k are getting cached into the KV store linearly per token and not hitting eviction fast enough. Our continuous batching keeps appending KV pages because the window paging code assumes bounded prompt lengths.

sre_pager: Is this a regression from yesterday's runtime change? We rolled a small batching optimization last night.

eng_runtime_amy: Possibly. The rollout toggled an aggressive batching heuristic: `continuous_batching.enable_dynamic_window=true`. It allowed longer prefixes to be concatenated into existing batches which avoids recompile but can cause unbounded kv growth if a single req contains a huge prefix.

ml_oncall_rajesh: Quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle incoming request token length at the router for hosted tenants 2) flip the dynamic window heuristic off 3) force evictions on kvcache for the affected pool 4) contact impacted customers.

prod_support_kim: I'm drafting the incident message for affected customers. For now mark impacted tenants: acme-*, beta-analytics, and public-demo.

eng_runtime_amy: I'll prepare the config flip. Adding a temporary rule to the gateway: `max_request_tokens=65536` and `reject_long_requests=true`. That will give us breathing room.

sre_pager: Can we do a hotfix toggle first rather than a full deploy? If the feature flag exists we can revert immediately.

eng_runtime_amy: Yes. There's a FF `dyn_window_v2` controlling the heuristic. I'm toggling it off across hosted pool-3 now.

deploy-bot: deploy started: ff-toggle dyn_window_v2 -> OFF targeting pool-3 (hosts=12)

eng_runtime_amy: Done. Confirmed flag is OFF on all hosts in pool-3.

ops_bot: Metric snapshot post-toggle (2m): memory usage on pool-3 stalled and dipped ~12%. OOMs still happening on a few nodes due to existing heavy entries.

ml_oncall_rajesh: Ok next: forced eviction. Running eviction sweep with higher aggression: `kvcache.eviction_threshold=0.6` and `evict_scan_batch=10k`. Pushing to pool-3 now.

eng_runtime_amy: Command I ran: 
```sh
curl -X POST https://internal-admin/api/kvcache/evict -d '{"pool":"pool-3","threshold":0.6}' -H "Authorization: Bearer REDACTED"
```

ops_bot: Eviction sweep started. Progress logs: evicted ~4.2M entries in first 30s, freed ~18GB memory.

sre_pager: Good. Monitor for churning — we don't want cache thrash.

prod_support_kim: Customer outbound: "We're investigating elevated errors affecting some hosted inference requests. We're applying mitigations; your requests may get rejected briefly if they're very long. We'll update in 30 minutes." Sent to acme and beta-analytics.

eng_runtime_amy: Also added a quick rate limit rule: any request with tokens > 80k gets 429 with a descriptive error and a link to docs. This prevents immediate reoccurrence.

ml_oncall_rajesh: I'm seeing the KV entry growth curve flatten now. Continuous-batching backlog reduced. Memory on worst host down from 70GB -> 52GB. No new OOMs in last 8 minutes.

sre_pager: Nice. Can we run a targeted load test to validate before marking resolved?

eng_runtime_amy: Spinning up synthetic load against pool-3 with varying prompt lengths, including a few 100k token tails to ensure rejects are applied.

ops_bot: Synthetic test results: 1000 reqs, 3% 429s for >80k token requests, p95 latency unaffected, no OOMs after 10m soak.

prod_support_kim: Drafting follow-up message: asking customers to trim prompts, use chunked input, or contact support for special accommodation. Will include mitigations we applied.

sre_pager: Handing off to ops rotation for postmortem and follow-ups. @eng_runtime_amy can you capture the root cause and next steps?

eng_runtime_amy: Root cause: dynamic continuous-batching window allowed concatenation of extremely long prefixes into existing batches. This created unbounded KV cache growth because we treat prefix tokens as cache entries and eviction lagged behind insertion in high-batch scenarios. Regression introduced by FF `dyn_window_v2` rollout.

eng_runtime_amy: Immediate actions taken (all completed):
- FF `dyn_window_v2` -> OFF on pool-3
- Gateway rule: `max_request_tokens=65536` and `reject_long_requests=true`
- Eviction sweep: increased aggression on pool-3
- Rate limiter: 80k token cutoff with friendly 429
- Customer notifications sent

ml_oncall_rajesh: Follow-ups / TODOs: 
- Add server-side guard to limit per-request KV entries (hard cap)
- Improve eviction policy to account for burst insertions from a single request
- Add telemetry alert for token-length distribution spikes and continuous kvcache growth rate
- Backfill unit/integration tests for long-prompt batching behavior
- Plan a safer rollout for `dyn_window_v2` with canary of <1% traffic and worst-case-length tests

prod_support_kim: I'll keep customers updated. If anyone needs me to escalate to account execs, ping.

sre_pager: We'll leave the incident open for the next 4 hours for monitoring and postmortem writeup. Thanks all — nice quick coordination. :thumbsup:

eng_runtime_amy: I'll create the postmortem doc and link it here once started. Preliminary title: "kvcache growth loop from dynamic batching heuristic -> hosted runtime OOMs".

deploy-bot: ff-toggle dyn_window_v2 -> OFF (confirmed), gateway-rule applied, eviction sweep completed.

ops_bot: Incident status: mitigated, monitoring in progress.

prod_support_kim: Notifying customers that we're in monitoring and will follow up in 2 hours with a root cause summary.

ml_oncall_rajesh: Taking handoff for monitoring window. Leaving note: watch mem, kvcache_entries, eviction_rate, 429-rate.

sre_pager: Handoff acknowledged. Closing active pager now.

ops_bot: System note: incident transferred to ops-monitoring rotation at 1769991800.

eng_runtime_amy: Postmortem link (placeholder): https://redwood.internal/docs/incident-postmortems/1769999999-kvcache-growth-loop (I'll populate details).

prod_support_kim: Adding customers to follow-up thread; will attach timeline and mitigation summary once we have the postmortem.

sre_pager: Great work. We'll reconvene if anything regresses.
